acceptance.criterion_verbatim: hyperlink clickability MEASURED, not inferred -- what markup the renderer honours. If it cannot be measured without posting, say so and stop; do not post to prove it.
acceptance.invocation: ast.get_source_segment on both send functions (the content-type is a hardcoded literal, so the question is settled at source and needs no call); NO Teams post was made and NO Graph API call was issued
acceptance.output_evidence: WHAT IS MEASURED: the send path posts contentType "text" on both functions, hardcoded, with no branch, no parameter and no caller override -- so no caller can request html today. WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THE VENDOR CONTRACT, MARKED AS SUCH: Microsoft Graph's chatMessage body.contentType selects how the content is interpreted, and under "text" the content is NOT parsed as markup -- so a markdown link [label](url) renders as its literal characters. THAT IS A DECLARED (vendor-documented) consequence of a MEASURED literal, not something I observed on the renderer. WHAT I CANNOT MEASURE AND DID NOT: whether the Teams CLIENT auto-linkifies a BARE URL inside a text message is a renderer behaviour observable only by posting a message and looking at it. THE TO SAYS SAY SO AND STOP, AND I STOPPED. No post was made; the gateway is also vendor egress and a send is not authorised here. >> THE ACTIONABLE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS WHY J2 PRECEDES TO-D: Andrew's ask -- 'hyperlinks (which should be properly linked to be clickable)' -- CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY A PROSE FORMATTING STANDARD ON THIS PATH. It needs contentType "html", which is a CODE CHANGE to a live EC2 service and therefore a deploy, not a style guide. A standard written today against a text renderer would specify link markup the renderer discards.
acceptance.denominator: 2 of 2 send functions carry the literal; 0 posts made; 0 Graph calls issued
acceptance.status_reason: PLANE: SOURCE for the content-type; DECLARED (vendor contract) for the rendering consequence; UNMEASURABLE-WITHOUT-POSTING for bare-URL autolinking, which is recorded as an open cell rather than guessed. Marked PASS because the criterion's own terms were met exactly -- it asks for a measurement OR an explicit statement that it cannot be made without posting, and the second branch is the honest one here. THE ONE THING A READER MUST NOT TAKE FROM THIS ROW: it does not establish that a bare URL is unclickable. It establishes that MARKUP is not honoured and that the autolink question is unmeasured.

My W-E SES leg is independently also plain text (MIMEText(body, 'plain')), and its CTA is emitted as a bare URL, which mail clients generally autolink where Teams markup would not render. TO-A's A4 asks for 'one standard hyperlink' -- on a plain-text body that is a bare URL relying on client autolinking, NOT a labelled link. Flagging so A4 is built with that known rather than discovering it at the first real send. No action taken.
